intertubercular tendon sheath: Sheath around the tendon of the long head of biceps in its groove; continuous with the joint cavity.
intervertebral disc c2-c3: Fibrocartilaginous disc between the C2-C3 vertebral bodies (cervical region); an outer annulus fibrosus surrounds the inner nucleus pulposus, spreading load and allowing movement.
intervertebral disc c3-c4: Fibrocartilaginous disc between the C3-C4 vertebral bodies (cervical region); an outer annulus fibrosus surrounds the inner nucleus pulposus, spreading load and allowing movement.
intervertebral disc c4-c5: Fibrocartilaginous disc between the C4-C5 vertebral bodies (cervical region); an outer annulus fibrosus surrounds the inner nucleus pulposus, spreading load and allowing movement.
intervertebral disc c5-c6: Fibrocartilaginous disc between the C5-C6 vertebral bodies (cervical region); an outer annulus fibrosus surrounds the inner nucleus pulposus, spreading load and allowing movement. The commonest level of cervical disc herniation; the C6 root is affected.
intervertebral disc c6-c7: Fibrocartilaginous disc between the C6-C7 vertebral bodies (cervical region); an outer annulus fibrosus surrounds the inner nucleus pulposus, spreading load and allowing movement. A frequent level of cervical herniation; the C7 root is affected (reduced triceps reflex).
intervertebral disc c7-t1: Fibrocartilaginous disc between the C7-T1 vertebral bodies (cervical region); an outer annulus fibrosus surrounds the inner nucleus pulposus, spreading load and allowing movement.
intervertebral disc l1-l2: Fibrocartilaginous disc between the L1-L2 vertebral bodies (lumbar region); an outer annulus fibrosus surrounds the inner nucleus pulposus, spreading load and allowing movement.
intervertebral disc l2-l3: Fibrocartilaginous disc between the L2-L3 vertebral bodies (lumbar region); an outer annulus fibrosus surrounds the inner nucleus pulposus, spreading load and allowing movement.
intervertebral disc l3-l4: Fibrocartilaginous disc between the L3-L4 vertebral bodies (lumbar region); an outer annulus fibrosus surrounds the inner nucleus pulposus, spreading load and allowing movement.
intervertebral disc l4-l5: Fibrocartilaginous disc between the L4-L5 vertebral bodies (lumbar region); an outer annulus fibrosus surrounds the inner nucleus pulposus, spreading load and allowing movement. One of the two commonest levels of disc herniation; a posterolateral herniation usually compresses the L5 root.
intervertebral disc l5-s1: Fibrocartilaginous disc between the L5-S1 vertebral bodies (lumbar region); an outer annulus fibrosus surrounds the inner nucleus pulposus, spreading load and allowing movement. The commonest level of herniation; a posterolateral herniation compresses the S1 root (reduced Achilles reflex).
intervertebral disc t1-t2: Fibrocartilaginous disc between the T1-T2 vertebral bodies (thoracic region); an outer annulus fibrosus surrounds the inner nucleus pulposus, spreading load and allowing movement.
intervertebral disc t10-t11: Fibrocartilaginous disc between the T10-T11 vertebral bodies (thoracic region); an outer annulus fibrosus surrounds the inner nucleus pulposus, spreading load and allowing movement.
intervertebral disc t11-t12: Fibrocartilaginous disc between the T11-T12 vertebral bodies (thoracic region); an outer annulus fibrosus surrounds the inner nucleus pulposus, spreading load and allowing movement.
intervertebral disc t12-l1: Fibrocartilaginous disc between the T12-L1 vertebral bodies (thoracic region); an outer annulus fibrosus surrounds the inner nucleus pulposus, spreading load and allowing movement.
intervertebral disc t2-t3: Fibrocartilaginous disc between the T2-T3 vertebral bodies (thoracic region); an outer annulus fibrosus surrounds the inner nucleus pulposus, spreading load and allowing movement.
intervertebral disc t3-t4: Fibrocartilaginous disc between the T3-T4 vertebral bodies (thoracic region); an outer annulus fibrosus surrounds the inner nucleus pulposus, spreading load and allowing movement.
intervertebral disc t4-t5: Fibrocartilaginous disc between the T4-T5 vertebral bodies (thoracic region); an outer annulus fibrosus surrounds the inner nucleus pulposus, spreading load and allowing movement.
intervertebral disc t5-t6: Fibrocartilaginous disc between the T5-T6 vertebral bodies (thoracic region); an outer annulus fibrosus surrounds the inner nucleus pulposus, spreading load and allowing movement.
intervertebral disc t6-t7: Fibrocartilaginous disc between the T6-T7 vertebral bodies (thoracic region); an outer annulus fibrosus surrounds the inner nucleus pulposus, spreading load and allowing movement.
intervertebral disc t7-t8: Fibrocartilaginous disc between the T7-T8 vertebral bodies (thoracic region); an outer annulus fibrosus surrounds the inner nucleus pulposus, spreading load and allowing movement.
intervertebral disc t8-t9: Fibrocartilaginous disc between the T8-T9 vertebral bodies (thoracic region); an outer annulus fibrosus surrounds the inner nucleus pulposus, spreading load and allowing movement.
intervertebral disc t9-t10: Fibrocartilaginous disc between the T9-T10 vertebral bodies (thoracic region); an outer annulus fibrosus surrounds the inner nucleus pulposus, spreading load and allowing movement.
intervertebral foramen: Opening between two vertebrae; it contains the spinal nerve and the dorsal root ganglion.
intervertebral foramina: Openings connecting the sacral canal to the anterior and posterior sacral foramina.
intervertebral surface: Surface of the vertebral body in contact with the disc.
intra-articular ligament of head of rib: Intra-articular ligament of head of rib
Joins the crest of the rib head to the intervertebral disc, dividing the joint into two cavities.
intrajugular process of occipital bone: Small process that partly divides the jugular foramen.
investing abdominal fascia: Deep fascia enclosing each of the abdominal wall muscles.
ischial spine: Spine on the posterior border of the ischium; the sacrospinous ligament attaches to it, and it guides pudendal nerve block.
ischial tuberosity: Tuberosity that bears weight when sitting; the hamstrings and the sacrotuberous ligament attach to it.
ischiofemoral ligament: Posterior ligament of the capsule; limits internal rotation and, with its spiral course, tightens in extension.
ischiopubic ramus: Union of the ischial and pubic rami; bounds the obturator foramen below, and the crura of the penis/clitoris attach to it.
ischium: Posteroinferior part of the hip bone (the sitting bone).
jugular notch of occipital bone: Notch that forms the jugular foramen together with the temporal bone.
jugular process: Process behind the jugular notch; rectus capitis lateralis attaches to it.
lacrimal bone: The smallest facial bone, in the medial wall of the orbit; the lacrimal sac lies in its fossa for the lacrimal sac.
lamina of cricoid cartilage: Broad posterior plate of the cricoid; the posterior cricoarytenoid muscles arise from it.
lamina of thyroid cartilage: One of the two plates forming the thyroid cartilage; they join in front to form the Adam's apple.
lamina of vertebral arch: Posterior part of the arch; it is removed in laminectomy, and the ligamentum flavum spans between laminae.
laryngeal prominence: Projection where the two laminae meet in front (Adam's apple); more prominent in males.
lateral angle of scapula: Lateral angle of the scapula carrying the glenoid.
